objective.text: Write a length in a smaller unit. Add and subtract metric lengths to solve story problems.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Feel the size of each unit
explanations.text: Use things you know to feel each unit. Think of a staple. Think of the height of a countertop. Think of the distance to a local landmark about 1 kilometer away. A meter stick shows the exact size of a centimeter and a meter.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Chart of units
explanations.text: A chart shows how two units relate. 1 kilometer equals 1,000 meters. 2 kilometers equal 2,000 meters. 100 centimeters equal 1 meter. 1 kilometer is 1,000 times as much as 1 meter. So the kilometer is the longer unit.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 2

explanations.title: Rename to a smaller unit
explanations.text: A length with two units is a mixed unit. To rename 1 kilometer 500 meters, change the kilometer to meters. 1,000 meters plus 500 meters is 1,500 meters. To go back, make groups of 1,000 meters. 2,500 meters is 2 kilometers 500 meters.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 2

explanations.title: Number bond of meters and centimeters
explanations.text: A number bond shows a whole and its parts. Take 150 centimeters as the whole. One part is 1 meter. 1 meter is 100 centimeters. The other part is 50 centimeters.

source_ref.section: Fluency Practice: Meter and Centimeter Number Bonds

explanations.title: Add and subtract mixed units
explanations.text: We cannot add different units. Rename them to one unit first. Then use the algorithm or a simplifying strategy. A simplifying strategy works well when there is no regrouping. To subtract, you can also count up on a number line.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Weight and mass
explanations.text: A scientist says mass. A 1 liter bottle of water has a mass of 1 kilogram. A dictionary is about 1 kilogram. A small paper clip is about 1 gram. A dollar bill is about 1 gram too.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Chart of kilograms and grams
explanations.text: A chart shows how kilograms and grams relate. 1 kilogram equals 1,000 grams. 2 kilograms equal 2,000 grams. 3,000 grams equal 3 kilograms. 1 kilogram is 1,000 times as much as 1 gram. So the kilogram is the heavier unit.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Rename kilograms and grams
explanations.text: To rename 1 kilogram 500 grams, change the kilogram to grams. 1,000 grams plus 500 grams is 1,500 grams. To go back, make groups of 1,000 grams. 2,500 grams is 2 kilograms 500 grams.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Number bond of kilograms and grams
explanations.text: A number bond shows a whole and its parts. The whole is 2 kilograms. One part is 1 kilogram. The other part is 1,000 grams. 1 kilogram plus 1,000 grams equals 1 kilogram plus 1 kilogram.

source_ref.section: Fluency Practice: Convert Units

explanations.title: Add and subtract mixed masses
explanations.text: We cannot add different units. Rename them to one unit first. Then use the algorithm or a simplifying strategy. Use a simplifying strategy when it is easy to combine the units. To subtract, you can also count up on a number line.

explanations.title: Capacity and the beaker
explanations.text: Capacity is how much a container can hold. A beaker has a scale with liters on one side and milliliters on the other. This beaker has a capacity of 3 liters. Look at the fill level to read how much water it holds.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Chart of liters and milliliters
explanations.text: 1 liter equals 1,000 milliliters. 2 liters equal 2,000 milliliters. 1 liter is 1,000 times as much as 1 milliliter. A mixed unit uses both. 1 liter 500 milliliters equals 1,500 milliliters.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1

explanations.title: Rename liters and milliliters
explanations.text: To rename 32 liters 420 milliliters, change the liters to milliliters. That is 32,420 milliliters. To go back, make groups of 1,000 milliliters. 46,005 milliliters is 46 liters 5 milliliters.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 2

explanations.title: Number bond of kilometers and meters
explanations.text: A number bond shows a whole and its parts. The whole is 2 kilometers. One part is 1 kilometer. The other part is 1,000 meters. 1 kilometer plus 1,000 meters equals 2 kilometers.

explanations.text: Rename to one unit, or add the mixed units. You can also count up. 32 liters 420 milliliters plus 580 milliliters makes 33 liters. For subtraction, you can rename 1 liter as 1,000 milliliters.
